decisions.issues: Clean. Dry Carnatic plain with rocky hills and a notch, the column winds toward it through dust, bullock-drawn cannon at the near tail, riders in dust-coloured quilted coats and dark indigo turbans, plain cream banners, no green, no red sashes, no faces. Very minor: one tiny distant banner near the notch has a few dark specks, unreadable at print size. Wide clear sky across the top for the caption. All checks pass (no text, no anachronism, no gore).

Costume continuity fails. The background riders wear white high-wrapped turbans, white trousers, crossed-belt vests and orange sleeves. That contradicts the bible's Chanda Sahib rider line (dust-coloured quilted coats, dark indigo or black turbans) and panels 1.1 and 1.3 on the same page. White turbans are also the Madurai troop's look, which the bible says these riders must never be confused with. Secondary: the lac seal has an impressed squiggly pattern that reads as pseudo-script on zoom. The framing is looser than the 'Insert, tight' direction, with a lot of busy column in the background. What works: a sound ringed hand, the navy-and-gold brocade kharita with gold drawstring, a red seal, the dry plain and clear sky at the top.
decisions.correction: Keep the ringed hand gripping the navy-and-gold brocade kharita pouch with its gold drawstring and red lac seal, the dry Carnatic plain and the clear sky in the upper frame for the caption. Crop tighter on the hand and pouch so the background is mostly dust, sky and distant hills. Any riders still visible behind must match the rest of this column: dust-coloured khaki quilted coats and dark indigo or black turbans. No white or cream turbans, no white trousers, no crossed-belt vests, no orange or coloured sleeves. The holder's own sleeve should also be a dust-coloured quilted coat sleeve. The lac seal is a smooth, plain blob of dark red lac with a rounded rim and nothing impressed in it: no marks, no script-like pattern, no emblem.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. The commander is on a dark horse at the ridge top with the sun behind him: heavy build, beard edge only, white jama, gold-shot cream high turban with a plumed jewelled aigrette, rich saddle cloth, no red. He faces away down the valley, so his face cannot be read. The banner bearer rides behind with a plain dark banner. Riders wear quilted coats and dark turbans, and bullock-drawn cannon are in the column below, consistent with 1.1. Horse anatomy is sound. Large clear sky at upper right takes both captions. The face entry marks the back of the commander's head, the key subject the captions should avoid, not a readable face. No text, gore or anachronism.

Acceptable with minor notes. The view south matches the script: forested Ghats slopes, pepper vines climbing a jackfruit tree, coconut and areca, flat paddy, a river, and a distant port with square-rigged ships at anchor on a glittering sea line. No terraces, no plantation rows. The commander is seen only from behind, beard edge but no readable face, and the quilted, dark-turbaned riders at left match 1.3. Minor issues: (1) the turban is plain cream with no visible gold-shot band or aigrette, and the jama has a plain sash, a slight costume drift from 1.3; (2) the near figure is lit and large rather than a dark silhouette; (3) the distant port has a few spires and towers, plausible for a 1730s Malabar port with European churches and a fort. Clear sky at top centre takes the caption. The face entry marks the back of the commander's head. No text, gore or anachronism.

Clean. Varma matches the varma-v1 sheet: face, curled moustache, red forehead mark, pearl earrings, cream-and-gold turban with jewelled peacock-feather crest, bare chest, gold necklaces and armlets, cream-and-gold cloth. This is the chapter 12 pages 1 to 4 formal court look, with no side knot or headband. He stands straight, gazes directly out, and holds the spear upright at his side; the butt runs off the bottom edge. Hands are sound. The Travancore hall has timber pillars, laterite bases, a tiled roof and brass nilavilakku lamps with open wicks, no throne and no audience. Clear sky between the right pillars and Varma, upper right of centre, takes the caption without covering him. No text, gore or anachronism.

FAILS the ear check. On v01, Nagoji's earring is a gold stud on the lobe with a second gold ball hanging directly below it (a hanging drop). Everything else passes: clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, barefoot with the boots side by side on the ground below the bottom step, sleeves down, talwar across his knees. Ramayyan matches his sheet and has the palm-leaf bundle and stylus. The shrine is laterite with a tiled roof, open-wick brass lamps and coconut palms at sunset. There is no text and the hands are sound. Secondary continuity problem: Ramayyan sits screen-left and Nagoji screen-right here, but the usable 2.4 (and 2.5, where Ramayyan's bundle lies to Nagoji's screen-right) has Nagoji left and Ramayyan right, so the page flips the 180-degree line.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's earring must be one tiny gold stud sitting flush on the earlobe with NOTHING hanging below it: no bead, ball, drop or pendant under the stud (the previous image dangled a gold ball beneath the stud, which is wrong). Keep everything else that worked: Kerala shrine at sunset among coconut palms, red-brown laterite steps and base, sloping tiled roof, brass open-wick lamps; Ramayyan thin with receding curly hair in plain white cloth, stylus in hand and palm-leaf bundle beside him; Nagoji in the rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves down to the wrists, broad red sash, cream trousers, talwar laid across his knees, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, bare feet, his brown boots set side by side on the ground below the bottom step. To match the next two-shot, seat Nagoji on the LEFT of the frame and Ramayyan on the RIGHT, with Ramayyan's palm-leaf bundle on the step at his far right side, and keep open sunset sky in the upper part of the frame clear for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Ramayyan's hair is swept back rather than the curly side-halo on his sheet, and he has light stubble, but he reads clearly as Ramayyan: thin, sharp features, receding hairline, plain white cloth. The wall behind is whitewashed while 2.1 has laterite walls (the steps are still laterite). The palm-leaf bundle reads a little like a bundle of sticks. The hands are anatomically sound and turning the stone (the beat). There is no text, and the sky top-right and the white wall top-centre leave clear space for the balloon.

Clean against all hard checks. The memory image bleeds in at the edges, as the script asks. Thatched village burning at dusk, rider silhouettes against the flames, a family on a bund carrying bundles on their heads, no bodies or blood, a plain unlettered dark banner. Minor notes: the woman wears a red short-sleeved blouse, and a tiny crossed roof pole on the right-hand hut reads as roof timber at print size. Clear sky top-left and smoke top-centre take both off-panel lines. Tails point to the left frame edge, toward Ramayyan in 2.2.

Hard checks pass: Nagoji's ear is a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, his chin is clean-shaven, he is barefoot with sleeves down, and he holds the talwar across his lap. The beat is right: Nagoji turned toward Ramayyan, Ramayyan looking ahead. Hands are sound and there is no text. Continuity issues: (1) the steps and pillars are grey granite, but the script and 2.1/2.2 have red-brown laterite; (2) the seating is mirrored against the current 2.1 (Nagoji screen-left here). The 2.1 correction asks for this order, so 2.1 will follow 2.4. (3) The boots stand on a lower step rather than on the ground below the bottom step (minor). Ramayyan's two lines fit in the sunset sky upper right. Nagoji's short line has to sit top-left, over the shrine doorway or the roof band. That space is adequate but busier, and it covers no faces.

FAILS the ear check: Nagoji's earring is a small stud with a larger gold ball hanging beneath it (a hanging drop). FAILS the no-text check: the saffron swallow-tailed pennant carries a gold emblem/glyph device that reads as pseudo-script, and the bible's Maratha flag is plain saffron. Also off-script: the farmer holds a straight-handled Western-style spade or shovel, not a hoe. Everything else works: Nagoji in left profile against the sunset, clean-shaven chin, barefoot with sleeves down, talwar held, boots beside him. The Deccan memory bleeds in from the left with riders in white angarkhas and pagdis, long lances and brown belts (no red sashes). Laterite steps match 2.1, and the open sky top-left suits both captions.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's earring must be one tiny gold stud sitting flush on the earlobe with NOTHING hanging below it: no gold ball, bead, drop or pendant under the stud. The Maratha pennant must be plain saffron cloth, swallow-tailed, with no emblem, device, symbol, gold embroidery, glyph or marking of any kind. The farmer in the stubble holds a traditional Indian hoe (a broad iron blade set at a right angle to a short wooden handle), resting it on the ground beside him, not a straight-handled spade or shovel. Keep everything else that worked: the full-width composition with Nagoji in left profile on the laterite shrine steps against the last of the sunset, rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves down to the wrists, broad red sash, cream trousers, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, bare feet, talwar across his knees, brown boots set together below him. Behind him, bleeding in from the left like a stain, keep the dry Deccan field with the line of Maratha riders in white angarkhas and white pagdis with long bamboo lances, no red sashes, and the farmer watching them. Keep the open sky in the upper left clear for two captions.

decisions.issues: Passes the hard checks. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, sleeves down, barefoot, boots set together on the step, talwar across his lap. The blue-going light and the shrine match the script beat. Minor: Ramayyan's stone is fist-sized and grey, larger than the small dark stone in 2.2. He also touches it with the stylus as if carving it rather than simply turning it. Neither is disqualifying. Balloon space: open sky upper left for Nagoji, and the roof and sky band upper right for Ramayyan's long line.

Fails the script beat: the action is swapped between the two men. NAGOJI throws the stone (arm extended, stone in mid-air), while Ramayyan sits still holding his palm-leaf bundle and stylus. The script has Ramayyan throwing while Nagoji sits still, and 3.1 shows Ramayyan holding the stone. Also not 'almost silhouette': both figures are fully lit and detailed. Nagoji's checks pass (flush stud, clean-shaven chin, barefoot, boots below), and there is no text or anachronism.
decisions.correction: The action belongs to RAMAYYAN, not Nagoji; in the previous attempt Nagoji threw the stone, which is wrong. Ramayyan (the thin, balding man in plain white cloth, no turban) sits at the RIGHT of the pair. His right arm is extended forward and up in the follow-through of a throw, hand open and empty, and a small dark pebble is a speck in mid-air arcing away into the dark between the palms. His palm-leaf bundle and stylus lie on the step beside him, not in his hands. Nagoji (rust-red turban, red sash, sleeves down to the wrists) sits at the LEFT, completely still, both hands resting on the talwar across his knees, arms down, only his eyes following the stone; he does not raise an arm. Keep what worked: the laterite steps, the tiled shrine roof with brass lamps, his bare feet with his boots set together on the step below, and the tiny flush gold ear stud. Make the shot truly wide and almost silhouette: camera low and farther back, both figures small and dark against an orange-to-violet afterglow with the sun already set, faces mostly in shadow. Keep the upper-left sky open and low-detail for one long balloon.

decisions.issues: Fails the script beat: NAGOJI is the one pointing at the hills, while Ramayyan only watches. The script has Ramayyan pointing and Nagoji following the line of his arm, and both balloons are Ramayyan's. The lighting also breaks continuity: bright golden late-afternoon light on the whitewashed wall and a sun still well up, against the blue dusk of 3.1 and the script's 'thin gold line along the ridge'. Nagoji's checks pass (flush gold stud, clean-shaven chin, barefoot, boots below, sleeves down). No text or anachronism.
decisions.correction: RAMAYYAN must be the one pointing, not Nagoji; in the previous attempt Nagoji pointed, which is wrong. Ramayyan (thin, balding, plain white cloth, no turban) sits at the RIGHT of the pair, nearest the hills. His right arm is raised and extended toward the southeastern hills on the right of the frame, index finger pointing, and his palm-leaf bundle and stylus rest on the step beside him. Nagoji (rust-red turban, red sash, sleeves down to the wrists) sits at the LEFT with both hands resting on the talwar across his knees, arms down, head turned to follow the line of Ramayyan's arm toward the ridge; he does not point. Match the dusk of the neighbouring panels: the sun has already set and the sky is deepening blue-violet. Light the shrine and the figures only by the brass lamps and the fading afterglow, so the last light is just a thin gold line along the ridge of the hills, with no bright daylight on the walls. Keep what worked: the laterite steps, the tiled roof, the coconut palms, his bare feet with his boots set together on the step below, and the tiny flush gold ear stud. Keep the upper sky above the ridge clear and low-detail for two balloons, with the pointing hand below that sky.

decisions.issues: Shows the script beat: the Aramboli lines across the neck of a pass at dusk. It has a deep ditch, an earthen rampart, a timber palisade with loopholes, sharpened stakes and a timber gate. The few tiny Nair sentries are bare-chested and bare-headed with topknots, wearing white mundu and carrying matchlocks. The sky is generous and the torches are open flame. No text, no anachronism. Minor notes: (1) three plain off-white pennants fly on the works and could read as white flags rather than a Travancore standard (silver conch on red); they are not lettered, and the upper-left one may be partly covered by balloons. (2) The topknots sit on the crown more than the front, which can't be seen at this size. (3) The frame is a clean wide shot; the bleed from the ridgeline is a layout matter. The speakers are off-panel on the shrine steps, so the tails go to the side edges: Ramayyan to the right, Nagoji to the left, matching their seating in 3.1.

Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin face, receding hairline with curly black hair at the sides and back, a faint cheek mark, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus. The thin, knowing smile is the beat. The hands holding the stylus and bundle are sound. There is wide, low-detail sunset sky on the right for the long balloon. No text or anachronism. Minor: the sun is still a sliver above the horizon, so the light is a little warmer and earlier than the blue dusk of 3.1. That is acceptable as 'last light'.

v01 fails two hard checks. (1) Ear: Nagoji wears a gold ball drop hanging on a link below his earlobe, not a flush stud. (2) Sleeves: his right tunic sleeve is rolled to mid-forearm and the forearm is bare, but the chapter 12 @4 bible row says sleeves down to the wrists. Minor problems: the Nairs carry flintlock muskets with cocks and frizzens, while the script asks for matchlocks. His far-side boot and stirrup hang in front of the horse's chest, which reads awkwardly. These pass: clean-shaven chin; boots; Kayal is a bay with black mane and lower legs and no white markings; Dhanaji matches his sheet (short beard, white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, no sash, talwar drawn) and is on foot at Nagoji's shoulder; the Nairs kneel among the rocks, bare-headed with topknots and white mundu; Chanda Sahib's riders wear dust-coloured quilted coats and dark indigo turbans and wheel away across the scrub; nobody falls; no text and no blood; there is open sky at upper right for both captions.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition, palette and staging exactly: Nagoji mounted on Kayal at left against the rock wall with his talwar out, Dhanaji on foot at his shoulder with talwar drawn, Nair musketmen kneeling among the foreground rocks, Chanda Sahib's riders in dust-coloured quilted coats and dark indigo turbans wheeling away across the open scrub at right, and open sky at upper right. Fix these: (1) Nagoji's ear carries ONLY a tiny gold stud set flush on the earlobe, with nothing at all hanging below the lobe: no ball, bead, drop, ring or link. (2) Both of Nagoji's cream tunic sleeves come all the way down to his wrists, cuffs at the wrist, with no rolled or pushed-up sleeves and no bare forearms. (3) His far (left) boot is hidden by the horse's body, or shows only below the belly behind the foreleg, never hanging in front of the horse's chest. (4) The Nairs' guns are long Indian matchlocks with a curved serpentine holding a smouldering slow-match cord, with no flint cock or frizzen.

decisions.issues: v01 fails two hard checks. (1) Sleeves: both of Nagoji's tunic sleeves are pushed up to mid-forearm with bare forearms, but the chapter 12 @4 row says sleeves down to the wrists. (2) Kayal: both bay horses show white on the face. The left horse has a white streak down the nose and the right horse has a white star or strip under the forelock, so whichever is Kayal is not unmarked. Minor: Dhanaji's pointing hand aims at Nagoji's hands and hip, not out at the rocks, gullies and hills. These pass: a tiny flush gold ear stud with nothing hanging; clean-shaven chin; boots; talwar at the sash; Dhanaji matches his sheet and sits on a rock wiping sweat with a cloth; Nagoji stands holding both sets of reins with the horses' heads down; late-afternoon light; the same broken ravine ground as 4.1; no text; clear sky at upper right for the caption and two balloons.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition, light and setting exactly: Dhanaji seated on the rock at left wiping sweat from his eyes with a cloth, Nagoji standing at centre holding both bridles, two blowing bay horses with heads down behind him, the rocky ravine and hills at right, and a clear late-afternoon sky at upper right. Fix these: (1) Nagoji's cream tunic sleeves come all the way down to his wrists on BOTH arms, cuffs at the wrist, with no rolled or pushed-up sleeves and no bare forearms. (2) Both horses are solid bays with black manes, tails and lower legs and NO white anywhere on the face or legs (no star, stripe, blaze or snip). Do not paint a bright highlight down either horse's nose that could read as a white marking; the horse nearer Nagoji is Kayal. (3) Dhanaji's free arm sweeps out toward the open gullies and hills at right, his hand clear of Nagoji's body, so he is plainly gesturing at the land and not pointing at Nagoji.

decisions.issues: Minor only: the town's two-storey whitewashed houses with red tiles look a little Iberian, and a white tower with a pitched cap near the centre could read as a bell tower. A temple gopuram and the walled gate keep it reading as a South Indian frontier town. Otherwise clean: a high, wide view from the hills of a small walled town at the mouth of a pass, green slopes breaking into the flat plain beyond, and a road through the gate and out the other side. There are no figures, no text and no anachronism, and a large open sky across the top holds the caption and three off-panel balloons, whose tails run off the left (Nagoji) and right (Ramayyan) edges.

Minor only: the ear stud is a slightly large gold bead but sits flush on the lobe with nothing hanging. There is faint stipple shading along the jaw, but the chin reads clean-shaven. His face is lit more by the night sky than from below by the lamp. Everything else passes: rust-red turban, cream tunic with the sleeve down to the wrist, red sash and talwar; a laterite parapet; a clay open-wick dish lamp (no glass); the vision column carries saffron swallow-tailed pennants, with riders in white angarkhas and white pagdis with long lances and no red sashes; no text. The starry sky at upper left holds both captions clear of the face and the column.

Minor: (1) A plain white flag flies on the far tower at top right. It is not the Travancore conch-on-red standard and could read as a surrender flag, so the letterer should place the second caption over it or it should be retouched. (2) Nagoji's turban has a long tail hanging down his back that the sheet does not show. Everything else passes. The view is high and behind, inside the same laterite fort as 4.4. Nagoji, seen from behind, pinches out the clay lamp's wick and a thread of smoke rises. His sleeve is down to the wrist, his gold ear stud is flush on the lobe and his chin is clean. In the lit doorway below, Ramayyan (receding hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle, barefoot) and Dhanaji (beard, white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, talwar) talk, small and unaware. There is no text. The dark sky and treeline band along the top holds both captions.

Acceptable. Minor notes only: the sun sits on the sea horizon, but a dawn sun cannot rise over the sea on the west-facing Travancore coast. Readers may take it for dusk, and no lettering says dawn. The courier's head cloth is wrapped a little higher than 'low', but it is plain and distinct from Nagoji. The lather on the horse reads partly as a dappled coat. The background flag is plain white with no text. The beat is there: a bearded courier in a dusty cream tunic and dhoti on a lathered, stumbling horse; bare-headed Nair guards in white mundu with topknots, swords and round shields run to catch the bridle; horse lines, palm-thatch shelters and the tiled war hall behind. No text, no anachronism, hands and horse legs sound. Clear sky at top centre for the caption.

Acceptable. Minor: the light is full morning daylight, brighter than the dawn in 5.1, and the shaking of the hand is not conveyed. The ola is a thin flat stack of palm leaves bound with cord, with a dark-red wax blob. The seal's impression is a blurred texture with no legible letters. The hand is anatomically sound and the courier's cream sleeve and brown waist cloth match 5.1. Clear sky at upper right for the caption.

FAILS: (1) Varma's war-hall look (bible 12 @5-) is wrong: his long curly hair falls loose to his shoulders, with no side knot above the LEFT ear. With his curled moustache he reads as a bare-headed double of Nagoji. (2) His spear leans at his LEFT side (the viewer's right), not at his right hand as the script asks. (3) The beat is wrong: Ramayyan is writing on a palm-leaf bundle with a stylus instead of breaking the wax seal on the courier's ola. (4) Nagoji's ear hard check fails: the ornament is a gold ball hanging below the lobe (a drop), not a flush stud. Passing: Nagoji has the rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar, clean chin and sleeves down, and stands apart by a pillar as the only turbaned man. The Nair chiefs are correctly bare-headed with topknots, and the lamps, palm-leaf bundles and plain coin tray are correct. Varma's seat (a low cushioned bench) also differs from the carved chair in the accepted 5.5. An extra map on the table carries no text.
decisions.correction: Keep the open coastal war hall with timber pillars and the sea beyond, the brass lamps on stands, the low table with palm-leaf bundles and the brass tray of plain unmarked gold coins, and the seated bare-headed Nair chieftains with front topknots, white mundu, shoulder cloths and gold earrings. Keep Nagoji standing apart at the back beside a pillar, the only man in a turban: rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves down to the wrists, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin. Fix these four points. First, Marthanda Varma must NOT have loose hair: all of his long black hair is drawn up tight into a single knot on the LEFT side of his head, just above his left ear, with no locks falling to his neck or shoulders, so he cannot be mistaken for Nagoji. He is bare-headed, with no turban, crest or headband. Second, seat him on a carved dark-wood seat with a red cushion on the low dais, with his spear leaning against the dais at HIS RIGHT hand, which is on the viewer's LEFT as he faces us. Third, Ramayyan holds no stylus and is not writing: he stands beside a lamp holding the courier's single thin sealed palm-leaf ola, bound with cord, in both hands, and his thumbs are snapping the dark-red wax seal. Fourth, Nagoji's ear ornament is a tiny flat gold stud pressed flush against the earlobe, with nothing hanging below it: no bead, no ball, no drop.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. Minor notes: the ola he grips is a thicker cord-bound bundle than the thin sealed strip in 5.2, and no broken wax shows. He appears seated at a table, while he stands in 5.3 and 5.5. The framing is medium-close rather than tight on the hands. The beat reads: big tense hands with knuckles hard on the bundle under a composed, unmoving face at the top of the frame. Ramayyan matches his sheet (thin face, receding hairline, curly sides, plain white cloth). The setting matches the hall: brass lamps, white plain flags, sea through the pillars, plain coin tray. The blank leaf and stylus on the table carry no marks. Hands are sound. No lettering is needed.

Acceptable with notes. Ramayyan still holds a stylus over his palm-leaf bundle, as if mid-note, rather than lowering the opened ola, but he is turned to Varma with the leaf held low, and the bundle and stylus are his sheet props. Varma's knot sits high at the back-left of the crown rather than squarely above the left ear: close enough to the war-hall look, and he is bare-headed with no turban, crest or headband, bare-chested, in a cream mundu with gold border and gold necklaces. He has slight jaw shadow. His spear stands behind his carved chair by the dais. Ramayyan matches his sheet. The hall, lamps, coin tray, seated bare-headed Nair chiefs, the guard and the sea view are consistent with 5.3 and 5.4, and the hall is still. No text, hands sound. Clear sky between Ramayyan's head and the centre pillar, with the roof above it, gives room for the short Ramayyan balloon.

All hard checks pass. Ramayyan matches his sheet (thin, receding curly hair, plain white cloth) and steps forward offering the leaf; Varma is in the page-5-onward war-hall look (bare head, hair knotted at the back on his visible left side, bare chest, cream mundu with gold border, gold necklaces, spear standing by the dais) and leans forward reaching for it. Hands are sound. Same open coastal hall, lamps and table as pages 5 and 6. No text. Minor only: the ola is drawn as a small corded bundle rather than a single leaf; background chiefs wear loose hair and beards rather than clear front topknots, and one small background figure has a pale head cloth; the coins on the tray read silver rather than gold. Lettering room: open sky above Varma for VARMA; the roof and rafters above centre-left for RAMAYYAN's longer line.

All hard checks pass. This is a wide shot from the front of the hall looking back, with chiefs in white mundu and shoulder cloths, topknots, gold earrings and no turbans. Nagoji stands still at the far end in front of a pillar, the only turbaned man. Nagoji is in the commander look: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, sleeves down, boots, talwar. The banners are plain cloth and nothing in the art is text. Minor: the two nearest left-hand chiefs face the camera and glance sideways instead of turning over their shoulders toward the back, though all the other chiefs do turn back. Topknots sit at the crown rather than the front, and the coins on the foreground tray read silver. The caption fits over the roof and rafter band at the top left, or the open sky above Nagoji.

All hard checks pass. Varma matches varma-v1 in the war-hall look: bare head, knot above his left ear, bare chest, cream mundu with gold border, gold necklaces. He sits on the dais reading the leaf with lips slightly parted and a closed, neutral expression. Both hands are sound. Same hall, coin tray and lamps. Minor: the leaf face carries faint, broken grain-like dashes that only hint at writing lines. They have no letter shapes and read as leaf grain at print size, so the leaf could optionally be retouched blank. The spear stands at his left side (frame right), not at his right hand. Lettering room: open sky to the right of his head (between the spear and the right pillar) and above his head under the roof.

All hard checks pass. The foreground chief is an older Nair chieftain (grey hair in a topknot, heavy gold earrings, white mundu and shoulder cloth) muttering sideways to the man beside him. His hand on his chest is sound. Varma stands in the background on the dais in the war-hall look (bare head, knot, bare chest, cream-and-gold mundu, necklaces), with the spear in his right hand, looking away and not at the chief. Standing with the spear fits the 'carried when he rises' rule and matches 6.5, where he also stands with it. Minor: a few grey streaks in Varma's hair (6.1 and 6.3 show it black); the small paper map on the table has tiny illegible scribble marks that read as map detail, not letters, at print size. Lettering room: the roof and palm area at top left for CHIEF, and the open sky between the centre pillar and Varma for his two lines.

All hard checks pass. The camera looks over Varma's bare shoulder: profile edge, moustache, knot on top, gold necklaces, spear in his right hand, matching 6.4. It looks straight down the hall to Nagoji, standing small at the far end by a pillar, with the chiefs on both sides leaning out of the king's line of sight. Nagoji has the rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny gold studs with nothing visibly hanging, sleeves down to the wrists, red sash, talwar and boots. Banners are plain. Minor: Varma's hair falls as a loose curly mass with a crown knot and a little grey, rather than a neat side knot. The coins on the tray read silver, while 6.4 shows gold. The paper map has tiny illegible scribble marks, unreadable at print size. Lettering room: the roof and rafter band at top centre, or the sky and palms left of the centre pillar, clear of Nagoji's head.

v01 fails the hard ear check. Nagoji wears a gold ball hanging below the lobe on a short loop, a drop rather than a flush stud. It also fails the framing: the script asks for 'Close on Nagoji', but v01 is a full-length medium-wide shot with Nagoji small in the upper left.
